description: List the machines this session can use: the ones the user added (name, ssh host, Slurm cluster or not, and a state only while this session is connected to it; `not connected` says nothing about whether Julia runs there), "local" (this computer), which one this session uses, and the ssh Host names not added yet. Starts no connection. Call it before add_machine or use_machine when the user names a server, and use it, not your own shell, to find the machine: do not read `~/.ssh`.
name: list_machines

description: Add a server or Slurm cluster login node that the user reaches over ssh (or update one added before), so notebooks can run there. Only when the user asks. It uses the user's own ssh keys and agent: never ask for or type a password. If it can't connect, nothing is saved; pass on what the result says the user must do. It installs nothing unless `install` is true, and never installs Julia: if Endeavor's program is missing there the result is `needs_install`, naming what, where and how large; ask the user, and call again with `install` true only if they agree. Waits up to 45 seconds; if it says it is still connecting, call again with the same host.

host.description: An ssh alias from ~/.ssh/config, or user@host, optionally with :port. Use the host the user named; if you use a different name from list_machines, tell the user which.

install.description: true: Endeavor may install its program there (a few files in one folder; not Julia). Only after the user agreed to what `needs_install` named; never on a first call.

julia.description: Where Julia is, if Endeavor should not look for it: a path to the julia program, or a shell line that puts it on the PATH, such as `module load julia`.

name.description: Name for the machine in these tools: letters, digits, - _ and . only. Defaults to the host.

slurm.description: true: run Julia in Slurm jobs (an error without Slurm). false: run it directly, even if Slurm is there. Left out: a new machine uses jobs if Slurm is there; one added before stays as saved. If the user hasn't said, leave it out, and if the result says Julia runs in Slurm jobs, check with the user before `use_machine`. Pass false only for the user's own workstation, or once the user confirms the machine isn't a shared cluster: on a cluster it runs Julia on the login node, which other people share. Refused while Julia runs there.

name: add_machine

description: Put this session's notebooks on a machine from list_machines, or back on "local". It attaches to the Julia already running there, starts it, or on a Slurm cluster submits a job for it. Only when the user asks. Returns within 45 seconds with a `state`. `ready`: give the user `browser_url` (it works while this session is connected); `remote_port` is Julia's own port on the machine: on a plain server the `message` gives an ssh command the user can run to reach it after this session ends; on a cluster it is on the job's node, behind the login node, and there is no such command. `starting`, `queued`: not up yet; to wait, call a notebook tool (each call waits up to 45 seconds); `pluto_session_status` answers at once and only shows the step, so do not call it repeatedly. `needs_job`: a cluster with no job running and no resources given; nothing was submitted. Show the user the `defaults` and call again with the resources they agree to; never submit a job with resources they have not agreed to. `needs_install`: ask the user, and call again with `install` true only if they agree to what the result names. A failed call, `needs_job` and `needs_install` leave the session where it was. Afterwards `list_folder`, `read_file` and `run_shell` act on that machine, and the session has no notebook there until it makes or opens one.

account.description: Cluster only: the Slurm account to charge.

cpus.description: Cluster only: CPUs for the job.

extra_sbatch_flags.description: Cluster only: more sbatch flags, each one string that starts with `-` and holds the flag and its value together, such as "--constraint=a100". `--wrap` and line breaks are refused.

folder.description: The session's folder on the machine: where new notebooks go, where a notebook tool's relative path starts, and where `run_shell` runs by default. Default: the project's remembered folder for it, else its home.

gpus.description: Cluster only: a count, or a Slurm gres string such as "gpu:a100:2". 0 means no GPU.

hours.description: Cluster only: the job's time limit in hours; the job and its notebooks end then.

install.description: true: Endeavor may install what `needs_install` named, and what this call then needs (such as Julia). Only after the user agreed; this call only; never on a first call.

machine.description: "local", or a machine's name from list_machines.

memory_gb.description: Cluster only: memory for the job in GB.

partition.description: Cluster only: the Slurm partition. Default: the machine's saved one.

name: use_machine

description: Stop the Julia runtime on a machine ("local" is this computer) for every client, and on a cluster cancel its job. This ends all notebooks running there, other people's too. Only when the user asks. Without `force` it stops nothing, and says why, if another session was active in the last 15 minutes, Julia is still starting or a job is queued, or it can't check: tell the user, and call again with `force` true only if they agree. With `force` a start that is under way is cancelled, on this computer too. If Endeavor's program there is missing or too old, the result is `needs_install`: ask the user, and set `install` only if they agree. This session stays pointed at the machine; `use_machine` starts it again.

force.description: Stop even though another session was active lately or Julia is still starting. Only after the user agreed.

install.description: true: Endeavor may install its program there, which stopping needs (missing, or only an older version there). Only after the user agreed to what `needs_install` named; never on a first call.

machine.description: "local", or a machine's name from list_machines.

name: stop_machine
